findings.title: GitHub user validation is bypassed when Integration record does not yet exist in the database
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist` (lines 475-482), the view immediately returns `pipeline.next_step()`, completely skipping the `github_authenticated_user` check at lines 501-505. If a victim installs the GitHub App and the `installation` webhook is delayed, fails, or is not processed before an attacker (or the normal setup flow) hits `GitHubInstallation` with the `installation_id`, the `Integration` record won't exist in the DB yet and `build_integration()` will create it directly from GitHub's `/app/installations/{installation_id}` endpoint without ever verifying who installed the app. Additionally, even if `Integration` does exist, `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` at line 503 will raise a `KeyError` if `sender` was not populated on the `Integration` metadata (for example, if the `Integration` was previously created via `build_integration` without a `sender` in pipeline state).

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` fails due to OAuth state mismatch instead of testing a 404 installation lookup
findings.body: In `test_installation_not_found`, the first request is made to `self.setup_path` instead of `self.init_path`, and the second request passes a hardcoded `state` (`ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`) that does not match `pipeline.signature` (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). As a result, `OAuthLoginView` rejects the request at the `state != pipeline.signature` check and returns `"Invalid installation request."`, never advancing the pipeline to `GitHubInstallation` or `build_integration` where the mocked 404 response on `/app/installations/{self.installation_id}` would actually be exercised.
